How to make QR code stickers

This tool makes the QR code file. You then print it yourself or send it to a sticker printer.

  1. Enter the link the sticker should open. Choose a link you control and will keep.
  2. Design the code: dark on light, with a quiet margin, and a logo only if it is small.
  3. In the download options choose SVG for a print shop or PNG at 2048 or 4096 px for home printing.
  4. Print a test sheet on plain paper first and scan it with two phones.
  5. Then print on sticker paper or order a run of stickers from a printer.

Sticker size guide

Bigger stickers scan from further away. As a rule of thumb, the code should be about one tenth of the scanning distance.

Where the sticker is scannedTypical distanceSuggested minimum code size
Laptop, phone case, product label10 to 30 cmAbout 2 to 3 cm (0.8 to 1.2 in)
Table, counter or menu30 to 50 cmAbout 3 to 5 cm (1.2 to 2 in)
Shop window or door1 to 2 mAbout 10 to 20 cm (4 to 8 in)
Vehicle, sign or wall2 m and more20 cm (8 in) and more

Choosing sticker materials

The material decides how long the code stays readable.

MaterialGood forWatch out for
Paper labelsIndoor, short-term useFades, tears and stains easily
VinylOutdoor, durable useChoose a matte finish to avoid glare
Laminated stickersMenus, tables and toolsGlossy laminate can reflect light
Removable adhesiveTemporary promotionsMay peel in humidity

Tips for stickers that keep scanning

Stickers live in harsh places, so build in a margin for error.

  • Use static codes for stickers. They cannot be edited later, so aim them at a page you control and update the page instead.
  • Keep contrast high. Dark code on a light background beats colored designs.
  • Leave a margin around the code when you cut the sticker, so the edge does not cut into the pattern.
  • Avoid curved surfaces that distort the code, or make it larger.
  • Add a short call to action next to the code so people know why to scan.
  • Test after printing, not just on screen. Try scanning at the real distance.
